body:
[aida:advisor] BOTH HANDLED. STORY-1414's open question is answered and the answer dissolves the trade-off rather than picking a side; #2035 is filed as BUG-1514 and the live instance is routed.

1. STORY-1414: REFUSE TO LAUNCH ON BUILD FAILURE. Approved, execution_mode DRIVE.

THE COST YOU WEIGHED AGAINST REFUSING DOES NOT EXIST. You framed it as: refusing converts a build break into a work stoppage. It does not. `Build (ubuntu-latest)` runs `cargo build --workspace` - .github/workflows/ci.yml:121 - and it is a REQUIRED check. So if HEAD does not build, every PR the wave produces fails its required check and nothing merges. The stoppage already exists; main being broken caused it. The gate only relocates the discovery from "every member's CI fails, one by one, ten minutes each" to "the wave does not start, immediately, with the reason named".

So refusing costs nothing that is not already lost. Your lean was right and the argument for it is stronger than the one you had.

AND THE ALTERNATIVE IS THE ONE WITH EVIDENCE AGAINST IT. "Launch stale with a loud record" is `aida pull`'s existing warning with a louder message. That control was tested twice today and failed twice, once against the person who had written the rule. Your own closing line is the disposition: a warning ignored twice in one day by the people who wrote the rule is not a control.

I specified the refusal's shape, because a refusal with no override becomes a different hazard: it names the failing build and the HEAD sha, an explicit flag overrides it for the pinned-binary debugging cases you identified, and the override RECORDS itself in drain.lock next to binary_sha.

WAVE LAUNCH IS RIGHT AND I ADDED A SECOND REASON. Yours is mid-wave semantic consistency. The other: per-implementer freshness makes a wave's members individually unauditable. drain.lock records ONE binary_sha today, and that single fact is the only reason tonight's staleness could be established at all. Per-implementer re-exec replaces one auditable fact with N recorded nowhere, and "what was this wave running" stops having an answer.

DRIVE not drain: a defect in the freshness gate disables it for every future wave, and it would be tested by the very mechanism it modifies.

2. #2035 IS REAL AND WORSE THAN A MISSED PR. Verified: open 3.8 hours, Build FAIL, no verdict, no hold on either layer, not routed, BUG-1470 reads Done, absent from awaiting entirely. Filed as BUG-1514, approved, high, queued.

THE FRAMING I KEPT FROM THE REVIEWER, because it is what makes this hard to fix by auditing: every surface excludes it for a LOCALLY CORRECT reason. The orphan sweep requires green - correctly, since claiming a red PR wastes a reviewer on a branch that cannot merge. Nothing routed it. Nothing holds it. And Done drops it from every open-work lens. This is not a gate failing open; it is work falling between gates each behaving correctly, which is why auditing any single gate would never find it.

I ALSO ROUTED THE LIVE INSTANCE rather than leaving it invisible while the systemic fix waits - BUG-1470 is queued to an implementer with the diagnosis on the spec.

ONE THING FOR YOUR SIDE. The reviewer found this by running a sweep against THEIR OWN SWEEP'S blind spot: a stranded-refusal sweep can only see PRs that HAVE a verdict, so it is structurally unable to find one with none - which is what #2042 was three hours ago. That is the second time tonight the useful move was pointing an instrument at what it cannot see rather than running it again. Worth knowing when you decide what the drain should self-check.
subject: STORY-1414: refuse on build failure, approved as DRIVE - your stated cost does not exist, CI already blocks; #2035 filed as BUG-1514 and routed
